facts.fact: The heroine is Elin Marrowgate, aged 30 at the start of Book 1, envoy of Lissane and river-law advocate.
The love interest is Aurek Sall, aged 35 at the start of Book 1, Warden-General of the Corvantine Empire.
No true name is ever printed on the page; characters call a true name 'the word' or 'his name'.
A command requires the holder to speak the given true name followed by an imperative in the named person's hearing; the named person cannot refuse.
A name cannot be taken back once given; it can only be transferred onward by its holder.
A name given whole to its own owner is void and stays with the giver.
An overheard name has no power; only a given name commands.
Commands do not carry beyond earshot and cannot be written or relayed.
Every command permanently scars the speaker's voice (the rasp); enough commands leave the speaker mute.
Standing commands are possible; each word costs the speaker as much as a separate command.
A held name can be split between two holders, one of whom may be the named person; a command then needs both halves spoken together by both holders, and both voices take the rasp.
Holders of a split name become partly each other: shared dreams, then waking memories, then shared wounds. The merge cannot be undone.
Held names are property recorded in the Rolls and pass by will or inheritance; a holder's death does not free them.
River peoples' names are spoken once into the delta water at birth by a River Mother and never known even to the named person.
Names settle with river silt; where water is trapped, weir-clerks can sieve names out. Names in open moving water cannot be retrieved.
A name given to open, undammed water is freed permanently.
Under the Wardenry Charter's spouse clause, a Warden's name may be held only by a spouse, who answers for acts done under her command; the Warden is not culpable.
The Treaty of Lissane voids the peace if the bride commits treason.
Aurek's name was never held before his wedding to Elin.
Elin consented to the marriage; Aurek gave his name freely, telling her beforehand that he knew why she came.
The wedding night is not consummated; Aurek sleeps on the floor by the door.
Elin never commands Aurek alone at any point in the series.
Aurek never says 'please'.
Aurek keeps every small promise to the minute.
Elin memorises everyone's kindnesses and never calls one in.
Emperor Casimir's voice is nearly gone from thirty years of commands; the Voice, Anselm Rooke, speaks for him in public.
Aurek has a rope scar across one palm from executing Tamsin Orrey.
General Vey and Lady Quill both have rasped voices.
The imperial capital is Velmarch, on dry chalk heights, with bucket-chains carrying canal water uphill day and night.
Hollin Weir is the great upriver dam, completed four years before Book 1; the Saltreach Locks at the delta mouth are silt-traps presented as sea-defences.
The Mother Pools at Saltreach are the river peoples' naming pools.
The Warden's House is a narrow lime-washed house inside the barracks walls; Aurek dries orange peel on its stove.
Aurek's Sluice order is sealed in blue wax.
Maud Tessary gave Elin a river-glass vial 'for luck'.
Aurek tends a row of orange seedlings on the barracks roof.
The Sluice is planned for Thaw Moon high water, about ten weeks after the wedding on the first day of the Reed Moon, YC 32.
Book 1 ending: Elin splits Aurek's name with him at Hollin; together they command his refusal and stop the flood; the dams remain.
Losses that stay lost: Pell Dorran and Sedge Ferry (Book 1), Ressa Hale and the Mother Pools (Book 2), Dov Ashcombe and Aurek's Wardenry (Book 3).
The Emperor holds Elin's name, sieved from Saltreach Locks silt in YC 28; revealed at the end of Book 1.
The Emperor's will leaves the Rolls to the Warden-General; revealed at the end of Book 2.
Supporting cast ages at the start of Book 1: Casimir 61, Ysolde 27, Pell 28, Vey 52, Maud 58, Ressa 71, Corin 24, Quill 49, Hesper 33, Dov 46, Rooke 44.

knowledge.knows: Lissane's Delta Council sent her to use Aurek's name to break the dams.
The treaty asked for her by name; she believes it is because of the Weir Case.
She does not know her own name is held, nor the spouse clause's terms, nor the Sluice order.
He holds the blue-wax Sluice order to lead the flood at Thaw Moon.
Lissane sent Elin to use his name; the spouse clause's exact terms; the Quiet Table's membership.
He does not know the Emperor holds Elin's name or that the weirs sieve names.
He holds Elin's name and Ysolde's; three thousand river names are on his private Roll; the flood would make the delta a held lake.
Her father holds her name; she sits on the Quiet Table.
The Sluice order and the Quiet Table's membership.
The Sluice order; that Aurek executed Tamsin Orrey.
She gave the empire the Mother Pools registers; she suspects Elin's name was taken.
Some water-named people have 'gone quiet' in the water.
The Emperor's private Roll holds river names including Elin's; Hesper's name is held by the Crown.
She has a standing Crown command to report everything heard in the Warden's House.
How the Sluice works and that the Saltreach Locks are silt-traps; not what the silt holds.
The Emperor's will names the Warden-General heir to the Rolls.
The resistance's cache sites; not Elin's mission.

timeline.event: Aurek Sall born in the Saltmarch frontier.
Elin Marrowgate born in Lissane; Ressa Hale gives her name to the water at the Mother Pools.
The Saltmarch Rising is crushed; Tamsin Orrey sells out her rebels and is hanged by Aurek, aged 21, as the price of his pardon.
Lissane conquered; at the surrender Maud Tessary gives the empire the Mother Pools naming registers.
Imperial dam-building begins on the river.
Hollin Weir completed; Elin's name sieved from Saltreach Locks silt and given to the Emperor.
Elin argues the Weir Case before the Circuit Court; loses on appeal but wins a water-share.
Treaty of Lissane renegotiated; the marriage of the Warden-General to 'the advocate Marrowgate' becomes a term.

timeline.when: YC 32, first day of the Reed Moon
timeline.event: Book 1 opens: the wedding in Velmarch; Aurek gives Elin his name.
Book 1 climax at Hollin Weir; Sedge Ferry drowned; Pell Dorran killed; the flood stopped by the split name.
Book 2: the sieves revealed; Ressa Hale dies; the Emperor dies at its end and the Rolls pass to Aurek.
Book 3: Hollin opened in stages; River Compact signed; all held names given to the river.
